prerequisites: Attainment of the second study section, requiring a minimum of 42 ECTS points from the first study section.
Knowledge of at least one high-level programming language that offers interfaces for using SQL

learning_outcomes.text: Name the basic principles and concepts of (relational) database systems and contextualize them as central technical and technological infrastructure components for data storage within enterprise-specific information systems.
Describe the basics of database architecture, database design, and database queries, and describe the most important associated concepts and abstraction mechanisms.
Assess whether and how these can be used to implement concrete technical requirements.
Formulate query and modification operations in relational algebra and SQL.
Understand the evolution of database systems from relational to NoSQL.

Apply the fundamental principles and concepts of conceptual and system-level database design to implement concrete technical requirements, create a suitable database schema for the requirements, and implement it in a relational database system.
Formulate corresponding SQL queries for technically formulated data queries and modifications and submit them to a database system.
Name the effects of different degrees of freedom in the design, modeling, and querying of databases and consider them when creating schemas or queries.

syllabus_topics: Fundamentals of database systems: History, concepts and architecture; 3-schema model and data independence
Conceptual (business) database design and Entity-Relationship model
Relational data model and relational algebra
Relational database design and normal forms
Advanced database concepts and thematic outlook
Conceptual modeling and design of database schemas
SQL: Data Manipulation Language (DML) and database queries
Handling incomplete information and null values

assessment_methods.method: Successful participation in practical course (four attestations)

assessment_rules: Passing the practical course (17.2) is a prerequisite for participating in the written exam (17.1). To pass the practical course, a total of four attestations must be acquired. This involves completing four assignments during the semester, with each successful completion earning an attestation. Solutions must be submitted on time or presented in a presence session, answering questions about the solution concept.
